title: URL shortener
summary: Map a short code to a long URL with very high read volume and simple writes. A classic warm-up that tests ID generation, caching and scaling reads.
requirements: Create short links, redirect on read, optional expiry and custom aliases.
Read-heavy, roughly 100:1 reads to writes; redirects under 50ms p99.
Analytics on clicks without slowing redirects.
components: API service behind a load balancer
ID generator (counter ranges per node, or hash + collision check)
Key-value store keyed by short code (DynamoDB/Cassandra)
Cache and CDN edge for hot links
Async click stream (Kafka) to an analytics store
tradeoffs: Base62 counter-based IDs are short and collision free but guessable; random IDs need a uniqueness check.
301 (cached by browsers, fewer hits, less analytics) vs 302 (every click reaches you).
Synchronous click counting is simple but slows redirects; async logging is eventually consistent.
body: **Estimates:** 100M new links/month → ~40 writes/s, ~4k reads/s average, more at peak. 7 base62 chars give 3.5 trillion codes.
**ID generation:** each app server leases a range of 1M IDs from a coordinator (ZooKeeper/DB row) and encodes to base62; no hot spot and no collisions.
**Mobile angle:** if asked from an iOS perspective, discuss universal links (apple-app-site-association) so short links open the app, deferred deep links after install, and link previews.
